explanation.heading: LESSON OBJECTIVE
explanation.text: Solve polynomial systems by substitution and check all real ordered pairs in both original equations.

explanation.heading: WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW / CORE IDEA
explanation.text: An intersection point satisfies both equations. A system can have zero, one, two, or more real solutions.

explanation.heading: KEY DEFINITIONS
explanation.text: Polynomial: an expression using nonnegative integer powers. Solution: an ordered pair satisfying both equations. Intersection: a common point of two graphs.

explanation.heading: CORE RULE
explanation.text: Isolate a variable, substitute, solve the resulting polynomial, back-substitute, and verify each ordered pair in BOTH equations.

explanation.heading: HOW IT WORKS
explanation.text: 1. Express y in terms of x when possible. 2. Substitute. 3. Factor or use the quadratic formula. 4. Recover y. 5. Check both equations.

explanation.heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 1 — PARABOLA AND LINE
explanation.text: For y=x² and y=x+2, solve x²=x+2, or (x−2)(x+1)=0. x=−1 gives y=1; x=2 gives y=4. Both satisfy both equations.

explanation.heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 2 — TANGENT OR NONE
explanation.text: For y=x²+4 and y=4, x²=0 gives one point (0,4). For y=x²+1 and y=0, x²=−1 gives no real intersection.

explanation.heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 3 — CIRCLE AND LINE
explanation.text: For x²+y²=25 and y=3, substitute x²+9=25. Then x=±4, giving (−4,3) and (4,3).

explanation.heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 4 — TWO POLYNOMIALS
explanation.text: If x²+y²=25 and x+y=7, then 49=25+2xy, so xy=12. Numbers with sum 7 and product 12 are 3 and 4; solutions (3,4),(4,3).

explanation.heading: DESMOS STRATEGY
explanation.text: Enter: y=x² and y=x+2. Look for: intersections (−1,1) and (2,4). Use it to answer: read both ordered pairs and check in both equations. Why it works: a shared point satisfies both graphs. Faster or not? Desmos is quick for intersections, but algebra is safer for exact radical answers. Check: (−1)²=1=−1+2 and 2²=4=2+2.

explanation.heading: COMMON MISTAKES
explanation.text: Do not stop after solving x; calculate y. Keep negative roots. Exclude non-real roots and check all candidates in both equations.

explanation.heading: EXAM STRATEGY
explanation.text: When both equations equal y, equate the expressions immediately. For a circle and a line, substitute and solve the quadratic; use the discriminant to count real intersections.

explanation.heading: QUICK CHECK
explanation.text: y=x² and y=9 gives (−3,9),(3,9). y=x²+1 and y=1 gives (0,1). y=x²+1 and y=0 gives no real solution.

explanation.heading: LESSON RECAP
explanation.text: Substitute → solve polynomial → back-substitute → verify. Report ALL real ordered pairs.

explanation.heading: NEXT STEP
explanation.text: Complete 18 practice problems, review 18 worked solutions, and submit the five-question test. Full English and Arabic instructional routes follow.

practice.question: Find every real ordered-pair solution to the system: y=x²; y=9.
practice.solution: Substitute y=9: x²=9, so x=−3 or 3; y=9.

practice.question: Find every real ordered-pair solution to the system: y=x²+4; y=4.
practice.solution: x²+4=4 gives x²=0. One tangent intersection (0,4).

practice.question: Find every real ordered-pair solution to the system: y=x²+1; y=0.
practice.solution: x²+1=0 means x²=−1, impossible over the reals.

practice.question: Find every real ordered-pair solution to the system: y=x²; y=x+2.
practice.solution: x²−x−2=(x−2)(x+1)=0. Substitute each x into y=x+2.

practice.question: Find every real ordered-pair solution to the system: y=x²−2x; y=0.
practice.solution: x²−2x=x(x−2)=0, so x=0 or 2 and y=0.

practice.question: Find every real ordered-pair solution to the system: y=x²+2x; y=3.
Find every real ordered-pair solution to the system: y=x²−1; y=2x+2.
Find every real ordered-pair solution to the system: y=x²+3; y=2x+6.
Find every real ordered-pair solution to the system: y=x²−4x+3; y=0.
Find every real ordered-pair solution to the system: y=x²+2; y=−x+4.
Find every real ordered-pair solution to the system: y=x²−6x+8; y=0.
practice.solution: Factor x²−6x+8=(x−2)(x−4). Both y-values are zero.

practice.question: Find every real ordered-pair solution to the system: x²+y²=25; y=3.
Find every real ordered-pair solution to the system: x²+y²=20; y=x.
practice.solution: 2x²=20 gives x=±√10; y=x, preserving the signs.

practice.question: Find every real ordered-pair solution to the system: x²+y²=13; y=x+1.
Find every real ordered-pair solution to the system: y=x²−5x+4; y=x−2.
practice.solution: x²−6x+6=0 gives x=3±√3; y=x−2 gives y=1±√3.

practice.question: Find every real ordered-pair solution to the system: x²+y²=25; y=2x.
practice.solution: 5x²=25, so x=±√5; use y=2x for matching signs.

practice.question: Find every real ordered-pair solution to the system: x²+y²=25; x+y=7.
practice.solution: 49=25+2xy gives xy=12; sum 7 and product 12 mean coordinates 3 and 4.

practice.question: Find every real ordered-pair solution to the system: x²+y²=13; xy=6.

test.question: A point satisfies x²+y²=25 and x+y=8. How many real ordered-pair solutions exist?

english.title: Objective
english.narration: Find every real solution of a polynomial system.

english.title: Meaning
english.narration: A solution is an ordered pair that satisfies both equations.

english.title: Substitute
english.narration: Set the two expressions for y equal.

english.title: Factor
english.narration: Move all terms to one side and factor.

english.title: Verify
english.narration: Check each point in both original equations.

english.title: No intersection
english.narration: A negative square target has no real root.

english.title: Tangent
english.narration: A repeated root can produce one point.

english.title: Circle and line
english.narration: Substitute a line into a circle.

english.title: Desmos
english.narration: Enter both equations and check intersection coordinates.

english.title: Recap
english.narration: Substitute, solve, back-substitute, verify, then practice.
